jobs.title: Director, Data Enablement, Data Platforms
jobs.description:
Purpose. Performance. People.

Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.

With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.

For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.

Role Summary:

As Director, Data Enablement, you will architect and evolve reusable enterprise platforms, tools, and services that help users and applications discover, understand, and securely consume trusted data products.

You will set technical direction for data portals, APIs, software development kits and consumption services; advance adoption across departments; and establish scalable operating practices, architecture standards and engineering excellence. Reporting details were not provided.

Accountabilities & Qualifications:

CPP Investments’ technology and data functions build secure, scalable enterprise capabilities that support investment, analytics, research and operational needs across the organization. The Data Enablement Team helps the organization derive value from enterprise data by delivering reusable platforms, tools and services, including the enterprise Data Portal, the FinSights BI Portal, low-latency consumption services, product governance capabilities and operational dashboards.

Accountabilities

Architect, design and evolve reusable Data Enablement services, with measurable outcomes for data discovery, access, trust and adoption
Engage users and stakeholders across departments to understand their needs, promote available services and shape a multi-quarter product roadmap
Design secure, resilient and scalable services using DevSecOps, automation, service-level objectives, observability and effective incident response practices
Develop high-level and low-level solution designs, including threat models where required, and obtain Architecture Review Board and Information Security approvals
Partner with Cloud Foundation, Data Foundation, domain teams and control functions to deliver solutions aligned with enterprise standards and platform guardrails
Establish architecture standards for portals, APIs, software development kits and consumption services that integrate with the Enterprise Data Fabric and data catalogue
Own the operating model for consumer enablement services while coaching Lead and Senior Engineers and strengthening delivery, engineering and operational excellence

What You Bring

10+ years of experience building and operating enterprise platforms or shared services, including web portals and API ecosystems
Strong experience with AWS cloud platform engineering, including networking, security, identity and access management, and multi-account environments
Expertise in API and service-based architectures, including REST or GraphQL, event-driven patterns, Neptune, OpenAPI standards, versioning, backward compatibility and resiliency
Hands-on experience with Infrastructure as Code and DevSecOps practices, such as Terraform, continuous integration and delivery, automated security controls and observability
Experience with solution architecture, platform governance, Architecture Review Board processes and Information Security engagement
Proven ability to lead cross-functional delivery, influence without authority, develop engineering talent and align stakeholders around measurable enterprise outcomes
Experience with structured data and schema processing; knowledge of semantic modelling, agentic frameworks, retrieval methods, vector search, container platforms or governed data-serving technologies is an asset. Relevant AWS certifications are preferred

You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment.

We provide colleagues with cutting-edge AI tools, dedicated learning time, and practical support to help them deliver with greater impact.

Inclusion & Accessibility

CPP Investments is committed to equitable access to employment and building a workforce that reflects diverse talent and perspectives. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Attention: Protect Yourself from Fraud

CPP Investments is committed to a secure and transparent recruitment process. We will never ask candidates for payment or financial information at any stage of hiring. All legitimate opportunities are posted on our careers page, and communications will come from our applicant tracking system, Workday.

CPP Investments may use AI tools to help screen and assess applicants by analyzing resumes and applications for relevant skills and experience. These tools support, but do not replace, human decision-making.

jobs.title: Managing Director, Technology Architecture & Governance
jobs.description:
Purpose. Performance. People.

Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.

With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.

For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.

The Role

The Managing Director, Technology Architecture & Governance is accountable for setting and governing CPP Investments’ enterprise technology architecture, As Managing Director, Technology Architecture & Governance, you will set and govern CPP Investments’ enterprise technology architecture, engineering practices and lifecycle standards, helping ensure the Fund operates on a resilient, modern and sustainable technology foundation.

Reporting to the Managing Director, Head of Technology & Data, you will provide practical, outcome-focused direction on architecture, technical debt, technology lifecycle management and engineering excellence. This enterprise leadership role has no direct reports and operates through influence, deep technical expertise, sound judgement and effective governance.

The Team

Technology & Data helps enable CPP Investments’ investment strategies and supports the Fund’s day-to-day operations through enterprise technology and data capabilities. Within the department, the Technology Architecture & Governance mandate provides enterprise-wide direction for architecture, engineering practices and technology lifecycle management, partnering across the Fund to strengthen resilience, scalability, cost efficiency and delivery effectiveness.

Accountabilities

Define and maintain the enterprise technology architecture, capability model and capability roadmap aligned to CPP Investments’ mandate, One Fund strategy, and long-term business objectives.
Provide clear architectural direction that balances innovation, resilience, security, and cost efficiency across the enterprise.
Lead lightweight, decision-oriented architecture governance focused on unblocking teams and resolving trade-offs, rather than enforcing rigid controls.
Provide timely, well-reasoned guidance on complex design choices, ensuring alignment across platforms while enabling local autonomy where appropriate.
Act as a senior problem solver for the enterprise, engaging directly in the most complex, ambiguous, and high-impact business problems and technology challenges.
Bring systems thinking and deep technical judgement to diagnose root causes, shape options, and guide decisions that balance near-term outcomes with long-term sustainability.
Own the enterprise approach to technology lifecycle management, including currency, obsolescence, and vendor dependency risk.
Define strategies to identify, prioritize, and systematically reduce technical debt, improving platform stability, maintainability, and total cost of ownership over time.
Set enterprise expectations for software development lifecycle, engineering excellence, and ways of working including agile practices.
Drive continuous improvement in how technology is designed, built, tested, and released, enabling predictable delivery, higher quality outcomes, and faster time to value

What You Bring

Undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field required
Advanced education or professional certifications in architecture, cloud, or engineering practices considered an asset
Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in technology architecture, engineering leadership, or enterprise technology roles
Demonstrated success leading large-scale technology decisions and standards in complex organizations
Experience in financial services, investment management, or other complex enterprises is preferred
Deep expertise in engineering, enterprise architecture, modern technology platforms, and large-scale system design
Strong understanding of cloud-native architecture, integration patterns, modern data achitecture, and security principles
Proven experience establishing and governing software development lifecycle, engineering standards, and agile practices
Expertise in technology lifecycle management, vendor strategy, and technical debt remediation
Understanding of financial services or large, complex enterprises and their regulatory and risk environments

You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment.

jobs.title: Director, Private Capital, Financial Services
jobs.description:
The opportunity

Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan Board (Ontario Teachers') is a global investor with net assets of ~$279 billion as of December 31, 2025. Ontario Teachers’ is a fully funded defined benefit pension plan, and it invests in a broad array of asset classes to deliver retirement security for 346,000 working members and pensioners. Our Private Capital group deploys ~$60 billion across direct private equity investments and private equity funds globally.

The Director will be a senior member of our Financial Services investment team — partnering with our Senior Managing Directors and Managing Directors to source, diligence, execute, and direct private equity investments in the Financial Services sector. This is a development seat with a clear path toward independent deal leadership for a candidate who has already built a strong foundation in private equity investing.

Who You'll Work With

Reporting to the Managing Director, the role will be part of a deal team comprising analysts, associates, principals, directors, and managing directors, supported by third-party consultants, operating executives, and legal and accounting advisors dedicated to each transaction.

The Financial Services team invests across sub-sectors including Insurance, Wealth & Asset Management, Lending, Professional Services, and Cards & Payments, with particular need to understand the regulatory, AI, and digitization themes reshaping the sector. The role will also potentially partner with colleagues in OTPP's global offices on international investment and / or cross asset class opportunities in Financial Services.

What You'll Do

Serve as a key member of deal teams — conducting industry and company due diligence, building financial models, arranging debt financing, negotiating legal documents, and preparing written recommendations for the Underwriting Committee.
Lead or co-lead individual deals and workstreams with oversight from the SMD or MD; own specific diligence streams (financial, operational, commercial, legal, tax, insurance) end-to-end.
Post-close, remain actively involved with portfolio companies — often as board observer or board member — working with management on strategy, value creation, M&A, and refinancing.
Contribute to deal flow generation through desk research, consultant relationships, operating executive networks, conferences, and relationships with management teams.
Lead sub-sector deep dives and thematic research as the team evolves its coverage strategy, including emerging AI, regulatory, and digitization themes.
Manage and develop analysts, associates, and principals on deal teams; provide direct mentorship on diligence, modeling, judgment, and communication.
Work in a highly collaborative manner, bringing a complex network of stakeholders along (Global and Sector SMDs, MDs, deal teams, Portfolio Solutions team, international office leaders, portfolio companies, etc.). Strike the appropriate balance of being a confident decision-maker and an inclusive leader.
Build a network of operating executives, CEOs, consultants, bankers, and peer sponsors; progress toward independent deal sourcing by the end of Director tenure.
Develop value creation expertise in close partnership with the SMD and MDs; contribute to portfolio company initiatives as assigned.
Exercise judgment within deal teams and surface recommendations to the MD or SMD; lead individual workstreams and, over time, full deals with oversight.
Provide disciplined thinking, sound judgment, and courage of conviction, with a willingness to take balanced, thesis-driven risk. Intervene directly and effectively when required and escalate issues early.
Work cross-functionally and collaboratively with other teams to ensure continued alignment with OTPP's mission, vision, and values — including supporting and sharing knowledge with other areas of Investments and responding to ad hoc requests.

What You'll Need

~10+ years of meaningful work experience, including several years of recent private equity investing. Active M&A in a senior role in corporate development would also be considered. Supplemented by previous experience in management consulting, investment banking, and/or corporations (preferably corporate development or similar roles).
Experience playing a lead role on deal workstreams, including conducting due diligence, leading multiple diligence streams (financial, operational, legal, tax, insurance), arranging debt financing, and negotiating documentation.
Direct investment exposure to Financial Services preferred.
Familiarity with Financial Services sector dynamics — particularly Insurance, Wealth & Asset Management, Lending, Professional Services, and Cards & Payments — and the regulatory, AI, and digitization themes reshaping them
Some experience serving on “for profit” Boards of Directors or board committees a plus.
Strong academic background, with a financial designation (MBA, CFA, CBV, or CA strongly preferred).
Experience playing a leading role in the investment process, including conducting due diligence, arranging debt financing, and negotiating documentation.
Strong negotiating skills.
Ability to balance priorities, work independently, lead projects, and thrive in a high-performance team environment.
Very strong analytical and quantitative skills to perform and guide in-depth, innovative, critical analysis.
Deep understanding of fundamental investment analysis and private equity value creation.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to build constructive relationships with internal and external parties, particularly management teams, boards, and senior advisors.
Strong communication skills, both oral and written, including IC paper authorship and presentation.
Willingness and ability to travel across North America and globally.

What We’re Offering

Numerous opportunities for professional growth and development
Comprehensive employer paid benefits coverage
Retirement income through a defined benefit pension plan
The opportunity to invest back into the fund through our Deferred Incentive Program
A flexible work environment combining in office collaboration and remote working
Competitive time off
Our Flexible Travel Program gives you the option to work abroad in another region/country for up to a month each year
Employee discount programs including Edvantage and Perkopolis

At Ontario Teachers', diversity is one of our core strengths. We take pride in ensuring that the people we hire and the culture we create, reflect and embrace diversity of thought, background and experience. Through our Diversity, Equity and Inclusion strategy and our Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), we celebrate diversity and foster inclusion through events for colleagues to connect for professional development, networking & mentoring. We are building an inclusive and equitable workplace where our talent is respected, accepted and empowered to be themselves. To learn more about our commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion, check out Life at Teachers'.

How To Apply

Are you ready to pursue new challenges and take your career to the next level? Apply today! You may be invited to complete a pre-recorded digital interview as part of your application.

Accommodations are available upon request (peopleandculture@otpp.com) for candidates with a disability taking part in the recruitment process and once hired.

Candidates must be legally entitled to work in the country where this role is located.

Ontario Teachers’ may use AI-based tools to assist in screening and assessing applicants for this position. These tools may help us identify candidates whose skills and experience align with Ontario Teachers’ objectives by analyzing information provided in resumes and applications. Our use of AI does not replace human decision-making.

To learn more about how Teachers’ uses AI with your personal information, please visit our Privacy Centre.
